newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Up to five said dead in Australian cliff collapse.
newsitem.headline: Up to five said dead in Australian cliff collapse.

text.p: Up to five people, some of them thought to be children, died on Friday when a cliff collapsed near the Western Australia town of Cowaramup, police said.
They said the cliff collapsed on a school group making an outing in a rural area. Others in the group were said to have been trapped in the rockfall.
"There would appear to be up to five fatalities," a police spokesman told Reuters.
Another police spokesman added: "There are no details available yet but there have been some fatalities."
He said a local school group had been involved.

The town of Cowaramup is in the Margaret River rural district about 200 km (120 miles) southwest of the Western Australia capital of Perth. There is a large national park near the town stretching towards Australia's western coast.
Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) radio said a group of children were still trapped after the landslide. It said several of the children were thought to have been seriously injured.
The radio quoted a police officer from the Margaret River police station as saying that rescue teams and volunteers were attempting to dig out the trapped group.
ABC television said there were 10 children and one teacher involved in the accident, which occurred as the group was walking under a cliff.
